_doc: The classification vocabulary for brokerage_transactions rows, and the
single source of truth for it: parser_common.py validates against this
file, Orby's pkg/ingest reads the same file out of the embedded scripts
tree to build its SQL, and tests/test_transaction_vocabulary.py fails CI
when a bundled parser emits a word that is not here.
WHY IT EXISTS. Money entering or leaving an account has to be
recognisable as such, because every growth figure is computed net of it.
Detection used to be a two-word allowlist (action IN ('Deposit',
'Withdrawal')) plus one convention (transaction_type = 'internal_transfer')
that four parsers happened to follow. A parser calling a contribution
'Contribution', 'Rollover' or 'Journal' had that money silently counted
as investment gain - no error, no warning, a portfolio that appears to
have earned its own deposits.
THE TWO FIELDS ARE NOT THE SAME KIND OF THING.
action           - the ISSUER'S OWN WORD, free text, for display. CSV
parsers pass the export's column through verbatim,
which is legitimate and which is why this field
cannot have a closed vocabulary.
transaction_type - the MACHINE-READABLE CLASSIFICATION, closed. If it
is set at all it must be one of transaction_types
below, and parse() rejects anything else by name.
SO: classify with transaction_type. The action lists below are a safety
net for rows that carry no classification - they are a convenience, not
the guarantee. The guarantee is that an unrecognised word is REPORTED
(Orby warns at import) and, for a bundled parser, FAILS CI.
_flows_doc: One entry per class of money movement. transaction_type is the value a
parser SHOULD set; actions are issuer words that mean the same thing and
are honoured when no transaction_type is present.
direction: 'in' / 'out' / 'sign' - 'sign' means the row's own amount
decides, which is what a two-way class like a cash sweep needs.
external: true when the money crosses the portfolio boundary. An
internal transfer between two of the user's own accounts nets to zero
across the portfolio and must not count as a contribution to it.
_non_flow_actions_doc: THE CLOSURE RULE, which is what the CI check and Orby's import guard
a row that sets transaction_type is CLASSIFIED - its action is free
prose and nothing checks it. A corporate-action row's action is lifted
verbatim out of the statement ('Merger Out', 'Assigned Out', whatever
the issuer printed), which is exactly why it must not be checked.
a row that sets NO transaction_type is classified by its action alone,
so that action must appear either in a flows[].actions list above or
in non_flow_actions below. A word in neither list is a word nobody has
looked at: CI fails for a bundled parser, and Orby warns at import for
So this list is not a catalogue of everything a statement can say. It is
the set of unclassified words we have already examined and decided are
not money movement. The way to stay out of it is to set transaction_type.
